fields.climate: temperate; hot, dry summers with mild, wet winters; harsher in interior
fields.terrain: high central plateau (Anatolia); narrow coastal plain; several mountain ranges
fields.hazards: severe earthquakes, especially in northern Turkey, along an arc extending from the Sea of Marmara to Lake Van; landslides; flooding; volcanism: limited volcanic activity…
fields.resources: coal, iron ore, copper, chromium, antimony, mercury, gold, barite, borate, celestite (strontium), emery, feldspar, limestone, magnesite, marble, perlite, pumice, pyrites (sulfur), clay, arable land…
fields.farm: sugar beets, wheat, milk, tomatoes, barley, maize, potatoes, apples, grapes, watermelons
fields.exports: garments, cars, gold, refined petroleum, vehicle parts/accessories
fields.industries: textiles, food processing, automobiles, electronics, mining (coal, chromate, copper, boron), steel, petroleum, construction, lumber, paper
fields.religions: Muslim 99.8% (mostly Sunni), other 0.2% (mostly Christians and Jews)

independence.event: republic proclaimed, succeeding the Ottoman Empire

fields.legal: civil law system based on various European systems, notably the Swiss civil code
fields.military: military service is compulsory for Turkish men 20-41 for a period of 6-12 months; men and women may volunteer
